issues.message: [family_confidence] Artifact family 'quotes' abstained at confidence=0.00 because quotes_missing.

[public_editorial_quality.semantic_review] The finance-app percentage changes lack an explicit comparison period, unlike the e-commerce changes. The bound source identifies the finance values as year-over-year changes.

[public_editorial_quality.semantic_review] The text asserts 2025 consumer spending rose 10.6% to $167 billion, but this item is bound only to the app-downloads fact. That binding does not support the spending metric or values; the separate spending fact cannot be borrowed for this item.

[public_editorial_quality.semantic_review] The e-commerce changes are explicitly year over year, but the finance-app declines and increases lack an explicit comparison period. The bound fact specifies year-over-year changes for finance installs and sessions; the comparator is not established for those clauses as written.

[public_editorial_quality.semantic_review] The e-commerce changes are explicitly year over year, but the finance-app declines and increases lack an explicit comparison period. The bound fact specifies year-over-year changes for finance installs and sessions too; the reader should not have to infer that comparator from the preceding clause.

[public_editorial_quality.semantic_review] The e-commerce changes are explicitly year over year, but the finance-app changes have no explicit comparison period. The bound fact specifies a year-over-year comparison for the finance figures as well.

[public_editorial_quality.report_limitations_omitted] The report covers the planned findings, but it presents several benchmark rates and retention/session measures without disclosing material source limitations: the verified facts state that sample sizes and/or underlying denominators are not provided. That caveat matters when readers interpret or compare the results, and no public item makes it clear. Dimensions: limitations: The source fact map records missing sample sizes and/or underlying denominators for multiple benchmark measures, but the public report does not disclose this methodological limitation for readers evaluating or comparing those measures.
